title: What does MPTokenIssuanceDestroy do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of MPTokenIssuanceDestroy and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, MPTokenIssuanceDestroy deletes an eligible Multi-Purpose Token issuance definition. [1]

Destruction has prerequisites involving outstanding token state; it is not an issuer shortcut for erasing arbitrary holder balances. Identify the issuance by its ledger identifier, not its marketing symbol. Reconcile holders and outstanding obligations first. Removing a definition does not settle an off-ledger redemption promise or convert remaining assets into XRP. [1]

The MPTokenIssuanceDestroy reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using MPTokenIssuanceDestroy, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
